claims.text: The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic.
The initial AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are well dispersed.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are crystalline at room temperature.
In situ AC-HRTEM during controlled heating can provide real-time, atomic-resolution observations of the nanoparticles' thermal behavior.
AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will retain a coherent, nearly equiatomic atomic arrangement up to a critical temperature.
The multi-element mixing in the nanoparticles is chemically disordered.
Entropy-stabilized disordered mixing mediates the retention of crystallinity during heating.
Nearly equiatomic mixing of five metals produces high configurational entropy.
High configurational entropy suppresses premelting in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy suppresses diffusion-driven phase segregation in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Suppression of premelting and phase segregation delays structural disordering or transformation during heating.
Below a threshold temperature, the atomic lattice will remain largely intact with minimal segregation or amorphization.
Stable lattice fringes and sharp electron-diffraction patterns indicate retention of crystallinity.
Above the threshold temperature, grain-boundary movement and defect nucleation will become evident.
The enhanced structural stability is limited to a high but sub-melting temperature range.
Above the stability threshold, diffusion, defect formation, or partial melting will occur.
Nanoparticle size, local composition fluctuations, and preparation methods may alter the critical temperature and rearrangement kinetics.
Diffuse diffraction and blurred lattice fringes can evidence loss of crystalline order during heating.
